title: Microsoft Purview: lifecycle status controls for adaptive scope recipients and site owners
summary: The briefing accurately separates Microsoft's planned lifecycle controls from the adaptive scope tools documented today. The supplied notice supports the defaults and rollout dates, and Microsoft Learn supports the existing commands, navigation and retention licensing requirements.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans explicit adaptive scope lifecycle-state evaluation controls for recipients and site owners.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Adaptive Scopes will provide administrators with explicit control over lifecycle-state evaluation for recipients and site owners

claims.claim: Administrators will control whether active, inactive and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in scope membership.
claims.quote: This update gives administrators explicit control over whether active, inactive, and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in adaptive scope membership.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The change is on by default for newly created scopes, which evaluate only active recipients and site owners.
claims.quote: With this change, newly created adaptive scopes will evaluate only active recipients and site owners by default.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Why it matters
claims.claim: Inactive and soft-deleted recipients or site owners will not be included in new scopes unless an administrator explicitly configures their inclusion.
claims.quote: Inactive and soft-deleted recipients or site owners will not be included unless explicitly configured by an administrator.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Existing adaptive scopes continue their current behaviour and are not automatically modified by rollout.
claims.quote: Existing adaptive scopes will continue to function as they do today and will not be automatically modified as part of this rollout.

claims.claim: Administrators will be able to update existing scopes to use explicit lifecycle status criteria.
claims.quote: Administrators will also have the option to update existing adaptive scopes to use explicit lifecycle status evaluation criteria for recipients and site owners.

claims.where: controls[0]; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No admin UI path or automation for the planned lifecycle status setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scopes lifecycle status active inactive soft deleted recipients site owners PowerShell Set-AdaptiveScope New-AdaptiveScope. Opened Adaptive scopes, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope; no lifecycle setting or parameter.

claims.claim: The query builder is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope > administrative unit > scope type > Advanced query builder.
claims.quote: Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... select + Create scope. ... first asked to assign an administrative unit. ... Select the type of scope ... Alternatively, you can select Advanced query builder

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <name> -LocationType User -RawQuery <OPATH query> creates a user adaptive scope using an advanced OPATH query.
claims.quote:
New-AdaptiveScope
    -Name <String>
    -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType>
    -RawQuery <String>
    [-AdministrativeUnit <Guid>]
    [-Comment <String>]
    [<CommonParameters>]

claims.claim: Scope membership is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Scope details.
claims.quote:
Select Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes.
3. Select an existing adaptive scope from the list.
4. From the Details flyout pane, select Scope details.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity <scope name> -State Added retrieves current scope members, and State can also select removed members.
claims.quote:
Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity "US Finance Users" -State Added
... The State parameter specifies the state of the members of the adaptive scope. Valid values are:
- Added: Current members of the adaptive scope.
- Removed: Former members of the adaptive scope.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: A role group containing Scope Manager can create an adaptive scope.
claims.quote: Any role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope.

claims.claim: The six listed built-in role groups include Scope Manager.
claims.quote:
The Scope Manger role is included in the following built-in role groups:
- Compliance Administrator
- Compliance Data Administrator
- Organization Management
- Records Management
- Communication Compliance
- Communication Compliance Admins

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The advanced query builder supports excluding inactive mailboxes with IsInactiveMailbox.
claims.quote: You must use the advanced query builder if you want to exclude inactive mailboxes. ... To exclude inactive mailboxes, make sure the query includes: (IsInactiveMailbox -eq "False")

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The advanced query builder supports targeting only inactive mailboxes with IsInactiveMailbox.
claims.quote: Or conversely, target just inactive mailboxes. For this configuration, use the OPATH property IsInactiveMailbox: ... To target just inactive mailboxes, specify: (IsInactiveMailbox -eq "True")

claims.claim: Learn documents IsInactiveMailbox for inactive mailboxes but no equivalent adaptive scope filter for soft-deleted recipients or site owners.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview "adaptive scopes" "soft-deleted" "filter"; Purview adaptive scopes lifecycle status active inactive soft deleted recipients site owners PowerShell Set-AdaptiveScope New-AdaptiveScope. Read Adaptive scopes and both cmdlet references; no equivalent documented.

claims.claim: Full directory is the default choice when not restricting the scope by administrative unit.
claims.quote: If you don't want to restrict the adaptive scope by using administrative units, or your organization hasn't configured administrative units, keep the default of Full directory.

claims.claim: The scope details State column marks current members as Added.
claims.quote: Review the State column in the list that shows Added for members within the adaptive scope

claims.claim: The scope details State column marks former members that no longer match the query as Removed.
claims.quote: Removed if the member was previously in the adaptive scope but removed now they no longer match the scope query.

claims.claim: Adaptive scope queries run daily.
claims.quote: These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Queries can take up to five days to fully populate, so Learn advises waiting before adding a new scope to a policy.
claims.quote: It can take up to five days for the queries to fully populate and changes aren't immediate. Factor in this delay by waiting a few days before you add a newly created scope to a policy.

claims.claim: The member details list can take up to five days to reflect added or removed members.
claims.quote: It might take up to five days for the member details list to update added or removed members.

claims.claim: The roadmap item and supplied notice describe no new identity or permission model.
claims.quote: This update gives administrators explicit control over whether active, inactive, and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in adaptive scope membership.
